newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NAPOLI COACH SIMONI TO LEAVE AT END OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NAPOLI COACH SIMONI TO LEAVE AT END OF SEASON.

text.p: Napoli coach Gigi Simoni, who has led the southern Italian Serie A club to the Italian Cup final, said on Tuesday he would be leaving at the end of the season because of a row over contracts.
"I asked for a two-year contract but they only wanted to renew me for one year. That's why I'm going," Simoni told reporters.
"The club did all it could to keep me and I also pushed in the same direction. But we couldn't agree on this point. It wasn't a question of money."
Simoni has, however, been linked with the coaching job at Inter Milan which will be vacant at the end of the season when Roy Hodgson takes over at English premier league Blackburn Rovers.
Napoli, currently 13th in the league, criticised Simoni last week for telling reporters that he had met Inter officials, although the coach had not given any details.

Simoni said he had only good words to say about Napoli, who have fallen on hard times since their glory days with Diego Maradona in the 1980s, and that, for the sake of the club, he was putting an end to the speculation about his future.
"I am just sorry to be leaving," he said. "I could be fired as I read in the papers. But I won't talk about that. I'm only thinking now about the league and the Italian Cup."
